item.title: Army Secretary Driscoll to Leave Post After Clashes With Hegseth
item.author: Jen Judson
item.content:encoded: US Army Secretary Dan Driscoll who has clashed with his boss, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, will be leaving his post, according to a person familiar with the matter, even as the military conflict with Iran continues.

item.title: Rep. Moore: 'Votes Are There' to Pass CR
item.content:encoded: Rep. Tim Moore (R-NC) says the votes are there to pass a continuing resolution that would keep the government open through mid-December. Rep. Moore says difficulty getting the 60 votes needed to advance legislation in the Senate has contributed to Congress’ reliance on continuing resolutions and says Washington spends too much as the national debt tops $40 trillion. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Scott Brown Was a GOP Star. Will It Matter in the New Hampshire Senate Race?
item.author: Jess Bidgood
item.content:encoded: Scott Brown is chasing the political limelight again with a seemingly improvised Senate campaign.

item.title: Supreme Court Allows Trump’s White House Ballroom Construction
item.author: Ann E. Marimow
item.content:encoded: Lower-court rulings would have blocked construction of the 90,000-square-foot ballroom after finding that the Trump administration should have first sought approval from Congress.

item.title: Trump Says US Could Still 'Smack' Iran
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump dismissed concerns that the conflict in Iran was draining American firepower, saying "This is a relatively little war for us." Bloomberg's Mica Soellner reports from the White House. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: India's Modi Calls on Putin to End War in Ukraine
item.content:encoded: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi called on President Vladimir Putin to end Russia’s war in Ukraine during a meeting in Kyrgyzstan. Putin responded that "we're moving in this direction." The meeting took place on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bessent Faces G20 Credibility Test | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 8/31/2026
item.content:encoded: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s interventionist summer has already led to pushback and questions about his credibility in financial markets. Now he faces a test with global peers. Ahead of the meeting of Group of 20 finance ministers in Asheville, North Carolina, on Monday, Bessent has vowed to return the conversation among the world’s top economic policymakers to the core subject of boosting growth. Shawn Donnan, Bloomberg Senior Economics Writer talks about the latest from the G20. Ed Ludlow, Bloomberg Tech Co-Host also discussed his interview with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Then, Brian Quintenz, KalshiEx Board Member and Fmr. CFTC Commissioner joined to discuss recent enforcement actions from the prediction market platform. Finally, Ryan Gould, Bloomberg News Deals Reporter discussed the latest on his reporting about how KKR has spent the past five years leveraging limited airport space to the advantage of Atlantic. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: 110 Trucking Schools Closed for English-Language Lapses
item.author: Karoun Demirjian
item.content:encoded: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, who has targeted truckers in the country illegally, said the schools certified drivers later found to lack proficiency.

item.title: Bessent Claims Canada Is Too Small to Fight a Trade War With the U.S.
item.author: Alan Rappeport
item.content:encoded: At gathering of G20 finance ministers, the Treasury secretary accused Canada’s prime minister of starting a “political shouting match” over U.S. trade policies.

item.title: Leader of DOJ’s Civil Rights Unit Spars With Harvard, the Left and Her Colleagues
item.author: Glenn Thrush and Michael C. Bender
item.content:encoded: Harmeet Dhillon, who leads the Justice Department’s civil rights unit, has extracted flashy agreements and personnel moves from big universities and sought to force states to turn over confidential voter data.

item.title: Bessent Takes Trump’s Economic Pitch to a Skeptical G20
item.author: Nancy Cook
item.content:encoded: Allies question the US prescription for global growth.

item.title: Kalshi Suspends Republican House Candidate for Betting on Her Own Race
item.author: Kellen Browning
item.content:encoded: The trading platform Kalshi issued a three-year suspension to the candidate, Laurie Buckhout, and fined her nearly $2,600. Ms. Buckhout said she had made a “dumb mistake.”

item.title: Supreme Court Lets Trump Keep Building White House Ballroom
item.author: Greg Stohr and Zoe Tillman
item.content:encoded: The US Supreme Court let President Donald Trump keep building his new White House ballroom for now, brushing aside conclusions by two lower courts that he is probably violating the law.

item.title: Trump Adds Nine Drugmakers to Medicaid Price Deal Program
item.author: Rachel Cohrs Zhang and Skylar Woodhouse
item.content:encoded: The Trump administration has struck new drug pricing agreements with nine biotech and pharmaceutical companies including UCB SA, Bridgebio Pharma Inc. and Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd.

item.title: House Faces Tricky Midterm Agenda | Radio Balance of Power: Early Edition 8/31/2026
item.content:encoded: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz discuss the latest between the US and Iran. On today's show, former US Army Europe Commanding General Ben Hodges, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino and Republican Congressman Rich McCormick of Georgia. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Russia's Putin Meets China's Xi, India's Modi in Kyrgyzstan
item.content:encoded: Russian President Vladimir Putin met with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit in Kyrgyzstan. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Dutch Government Clinches Budget Deal, Averting Political Crisis
item.author: Patrick Van Oosterom
item.content:encoded: The ruling Dutch coalition parties reached a last-minute agreement on its first annual budget, averting a fresh political crisis for centrist Prime Minister Rob Jetten’s six-month-old minority government.

item.title: Bessent Meets With Russia Finance Chief at G20 Gathering
item.author: Bloomberg News
item.content:encoded: Russian Finance Minister Anton Siluanov and US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent met on the sidelines of a Group of 20 gathering in Asheville, North Carolina, the Russian government said in a statement.

item.title: EU Nations Push to Give the Bloc More Foreign Policy Leverage
item.author: Andrea Palasciano
item.content:encoded: Eight European Union countries including Germany and France are stepping up efforts to overhaul how the bloc makes foreign policy decisions in order to allow the EU to better defend its values and interests.

item.title: Why the Times/Siena Poll Isn’t Hanging Up the Phone
item.author: Nate Cohn
item.content:encoded: Reader mailbag: The traditional use of phones in Times/Siena surveys is far from perfect, but its strengths shouldn’t be overlooked.

item.title: Plan petrolero de Trump en Venezuela enfrenta grandes dudas
item.author: Mie Dahl
item.content:encoded: El presidente de EE.UU. presenta su acuerdo por 65.000 millones de barriles de petróleo venezolano como una victoria. Pero las dudas sobre inversión, infraestructura y plazos amenazan sus promesas.

item.title: Do D.E.I. Bike Paths Exist? The Trump Administration Says Yes.
item.author: Richard Fausset and Alex Kent
item.content:encoded: The administration has revoked funding for bike paths, and encouraged removing some. A cycling advocate said it is playing on the idea of “that dork on a bike.”

item.title: A $480,000-a-Year Pill Reflects a New Normal for Cancer Drugs
item.author: Rebecca Robbins
item.content:encoded: Rasonque, the new pancreatic cancer treatment from Revolution Medicines, illustrates the huge inflation in cancer drug prices over the past two decades.

item.title: Senators Condemn Roblox, Discord Moving Victims Into Arbitration
item.author: Cecilia D'Anastasio
item.content:encoded: Three US Senators argued in court that sex abuse victims suing Roblox Corp. and Discord Inc. “deserve their day in court,” and shouldn’t be compelled into private arbitration.

item.title: Russia's Putin in Kyrgyzstan for SCO Summit
item.content:encoded: Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan on Sunday to take part in the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit. It's billed as a group that counters US global influence. He'll meet with leaders from China and India. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Says ‘Let Data Reign’ in Response to Data Center Blowback
item.author: Skylar Woodhouse, Dawn Lim and Maggie Eastland
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump warned that a growing public backlash to data centers in the US poses an economic threat to communities that oppose new infrastructure needed to power artificial intelligence and risks giving China the upper hand in the AI race.

item.title: ‘The Least Transparent Midterm’: How Dark Money Is Washing Over the 2026 Election
item.author: Shane Goldmacher and Theodore Schleifer
item.content:encoded: At least $1 billion from anonymous donors is flowing into the midterm elections. Dark money is not new, but it now permeates nearly every major contest.

item.title: More Mail Ballots Are Arriving Late This Year, and They’re Getting Tossed
item.author: Adam Sella and Nick Corasaniti
item.content:encoded: State officials say they worry about the Postal Service’s ability to deliver votes this fall. They are urging voters to mail their ballots early or use drop boxes so their votes count.

item.title: Pakistan Says More Muslim Nations Keen to Join Defense Pact
item.author: Tooba Khan and Beril Akman
item.content:encoded: Pakistan said six to seven Muslim-majority countries are interested in joining the Mecca Defense Agreement, as top diplomats from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey met in Istanbul on Monday to discuss security and military cooperation.

item.title: U.S. Attacks Island in Strait of Hormuz; Iran Retaliates With Missile Fire
item.author: Eric Schmitt
item.content:encoded: The exchange on Sunday was the first known military action between the two nations in a month, raising the risk of a renewed round of fighting.

item.title: How Trump’s Policy Agenda Runs Through One Federal Court, in Texas
item.author: Zach Montague and Mattathias Schwartz
item.content:encoded: For years, conservative litigants flocked to Judge Reed O’Connor’s district. Now, North Texas has become a favorite destination of the Justice Department.

item.title: Ed Markey Defends Transgender Athletes in Massachusetts Senate Race
item.author: Reid J. Epstein
item.content:encoded: Senator Ed Markey of Massachusetts has emerged as a vocal defender of transgender rights as he tries to fend off a primary challenge from Representative Seth Moulton.

item.title: US Treasury Bars Reporters From Some Outlets From G20 Summit
item.author: Bloomberg News
item.content:encoded: The US Treasury Department excluded journalists from several media outlets, including Bloomberg News and the Wall Street Journal, from coverage of this week’s Group of 20 finance ministers summit in Asheville, North Carolina, amid global market volatility and the US-Iran conflict.

item.title: Why the United States Can’t Quit Its Wars
item.author: Greg Jaffe
item.content:encoded: The country’s longest war came to an end exactly five years ago. Today it offers lessons for policymakers seeking to avoid an endless war in Iran.

item.title: Postal Service Rule Could Bar Millions From Voting by Mail
item.author: Reid J. Epstein
item.content:encoded: A judge temporarily blocked the agency from implementing a strict new rule governing mail voting. The policy could disproportionately affect Democrats and many battleground elections.

item.title: Trump Says Venezuelan Oil Will Refill U.S. Stockpiles, but It’s Not So Simple
item.author: Rebecca F. Elliott
item.content:encoded: New projects can take years to produce meaningful amounts of oil, and that’s especially true in Venezuela, where infrastructure is in disrepair.

item.title: Senate Passes Funding Bill Ignoring Trump’s Priorities
item.author: Erik Wasson
item.content:encoded: The US Senate passed a short-term spending bill to avert a damaging government shutdown weeks before the November midterms, sidestepping President Donald Trump’s calls to also enact emergency funds for the Iran war and elements of a controversial voter identification proposal.
